{"design":"PLAN (2026-11-02, awaiting Mark). Decision .4.65: committers refuse to commit while holding a §4.7-invalid stored AppDataUpdate, and protocol-06 §3.5 forces cached proposals into the next Commit, so the hub must refuse such a standalone proposal on arrival or the room's next Commit can never succeed.
Hub-only (no mimi-mls change, no shared test helpers), so it can run alongside the running agents:
1. components.rs: expose the set apply_commit_op accepts (hub-tracked + room_metadata + franking_agent) as one fn, used by apply_commit_op and the new check, so the two cannot drift.
2. update.rs stage_proposals: for each AppDataUpdate in the batch, refuse (existing refuse() path, nothing stored) when (a) its component is unknown to the hub, (b) it is a remove and the room's current dictionary has no data for that component, (c) together with the epoch's cached proposals and earlier ones in the batch it makes two removes, or a remove and an update, for one component_id (mls-extensions-10 §4.7 list rules). Update-content validity beyond that stays where it is (room policy decode).
3. mod.rs: Room keeps the current epoch's AppDataUpdate ops per component_id next to , extended on accept, cleared when a Commit merges, rebuilt in rebuild() from the replayed proposals (decision .6.6), so (c) sees proposals cached before a restart.
4. Tests first (new tests/hub_app_data_update_proposals.rs), proposals built by a plain OpenMLS client (propose_app_data_update, independent of mimid's Member code) in a hub room: unknown component refused; remove of absent component refused; remove then update of the same component across two separate submissions refused; two removes refused; a valid update accepted and committable; the cache survives a hub restart (refusal after rebuild). Each asserts the proposal was not stored."}
